Sauteed Mushrooms and Leeks

By: Author Kate Vaynshteyn

This quick and easy recipe for Sauteed Mushrooms with Leeks makes a great side dish that pairs well with chicken, steak, or fish. It's full of savory umami flavor and is very easy to make. It can also be transformed into soup, quiche, or into a fancy broiled side dish!

Sauteed leeks side dish

Leeks are such a great flavor booster for so many dishes. They can be used as a direct substitute for onions in most soup recipes, such as my asparagus leek soup and my butternut squash leek soup. But leeks can also be the main star! Or a co-star, in this case, since leeks are working together with mushrooms in this side dish.

This is a simple recipe with just 5 main ingredients so the leeks and mushrooms have a chance to shine. The trick here is to not overcrowd the pan too much when you're sauteing and let the leeks and mushrooms caramelize a little.

These sauteed leeks with mushrooms make a great side dish for chicken, steak, or seafood. And you can even spruce them up a bit by topping with buttered panko breadcrumbs or grated Parmesan and broiling the whole thing for a minute. It's an easy restaurant-worthy dish to make at home!

More recipes with leeks: Sweet Potato Leek Soup

Ingredients

  • 1-2 leeks, to taste (it's up to you how many leeks you want in this dish. The leeks cook down a lot and just add a nice savory flavor. Use 1 or 2 leeks, use just the white parts or both the white and green parts. I used 1 full leek, both white and green parts)
  • 1 pound mushrooms, such as baby bella, sliced
  • Optional: ¼ cup dry white wine
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter or oil of your choice
  • ½ teaspoon each salt and pepper
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves (or ⅓ - ½ tablespoon dried thyme)

More mushroom side dishes: Skillet Potatoes with Mushrooms

Equipment

  • Large skillet with a lid
  • Salad spinner

Instructions

Thinly slice the leeks (discard any tough or dry green parts) and wash them thoroughly to remove all sand and dirt from in between the layers. Pat them dry or use a salad spinner. I like to rinse leeks 3 times in a salad spinner, letting the dirt settle to the bottom before lifting up the colander part, then spin them dry.

Clean the mushrooms (rub off any dirt or quickly rinse them under water without soaking), then slice. 

Preheat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the butter, washed and dried sliced leeks, and sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cover for 2-3 minutes so they shrink down in size a bit, then uncover and stir. Continue cooking uncovered over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes, or until cooked to your liking. The veggies will release liquid, but continue cooking until the liquid cooks off and the mushrooms and leek start to caramelize.

Optional: Deglaze the pan with ¼ cup dry white wine, stirring all the browned bits into the veggies. Cook for 1-2 minutes longer to let the wine cook off.

Season with salt, pepper, and thyme to taste and enjoy... OR transfer to a broiler-safe dish, top with freshly grated Parmesan OR with a mixture of panko breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, and melted butter. Broil for 1-2 minutes, or until golden on top. Remove from heat immediately and enjoy! 

Recipe tips and variations

  • If doubling the recipe, I recommend using 2 large skillets so the mushrooms get a chance to brown. Otherwise they'll be stewing in their liquid for a long time.
  • If you have time, let the mushrooms sit out uncovered for 30-60 minutes to dry after washing.
  • Leftover mushroom and leeks can be added to an egg mixture to make a mushroom quiche or this mushroom leek soup. If you're planning on making soup or quiche, I recommend doubling the recipe so you have more mushroom mixture to work with.
  • Fun topping ideas to try: Transfer cooked mushrooms and leeks to a broiler-safe dish. Top with grated Parmesan and broil for 1-2 minutes, or until the cheese melts and starts turning golden brown. WATCH it carefully so it doesn't burn! Another fun topping idea: mix panko breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese with melted butter. Sprinkle over the mushrooms and leeks in a broiler-safe dish, broil for 1 minute or until the breadcrumbs are toasted (don't let it burn!).

What to serve with mushrooms and leeks

Mushrooms always make a great side dish for steak (try this air fryer filet mignon!) and grilled chicken breast. I wouldn't hesitate to serve pan-fried salmon steaks with these mushrooms either! Since mushrooms and leek would count as the "vegetable side dish" part of my dinner, I would serve them with another starchy side dish, such as mashed or roasted young potatoes or a side of fluffy bone broth rice. But for a lighter dinner, you can serve some roasted or air fried veggies instead of carbs. This air fryer delicata squash is great in the Fall, and roasted cauliflower is a great option year round.

Sauteed Mushrooms and Leeks

A quick and easy side dish that pairs well with steak, chicken, or fish. Totally customizable with your favorite mushrooms and however many leeks you want to ue.

Cook Time20 minutes mins
Total Time35 minutes mins
Course: Side Dish
Cuisine: American

Servings: 4

Ingredients

  • 1-2 leeks (leeks cook down a lot and add a nice savory flavor. Use 1 or 2 leeks. Use just the white parts OR both the white and green parts. I used 1 full leek, both white and green parts.)
  • 1 pound mushrooms such as baby bella, sliced
  • ¼ cup dry white wine optional
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter or oil of your choice
  • ½ teaspoon salt and pepper each
  • 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves (or ⅓ - ½ tablespoon dried thyme)

Special equipment

  • Large skillet with a lid
  • Salad spinner

Instructions

  • Thinly slice the leeks (discard any tough or dry green parts, but it's up to you whether to use the smooth green parts) and wash them thoroughly to remove all sand and dirt from in between the layers. Pat them dry or use a salad spinner. I like to rinse leeks 3 times in a salad spinner, letting the dirt settle to the bottom each time before lifting up the colander part, then spin them dry.
  • Clean the mushrooms (rub off any dirt or quickly rinse them under water without soaking), then slice.
  • Preheat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the butter, washed and dried sliced leeks, and sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cover for 2-3 minutes so they shrink down in size a bit, then uncover and stir. Continue cooking uncovered over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes, or until cooked to your liking. The veggies will release liquid, but continue cooking until the liquid cooks off and the mushrooms and leek start to caramelize.
  • Optional: Deglaze the pan with ¼ cup dry white wine, stirring all the browned bits into the veggies. Cook for 1-2 minutes longer to let the wine cook off.
  • Season with salt, pepper, and thyme to taste and enjoy! Or try the broiled version below:
  • Broiled option 1 (Parmesan): Transfer cooked mushrooms and leeks to a broiler-safe dish. Top with grated Parmesan and broil for 1-2 minutes, or until the cheese melts and starts turning golden brown. WATCH it carefully so it doesn't burn!
    Broiled option 2 (breadcrumbs): In a small bowl, mix panko breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese with melted better. Sprinkle over the mushrooms and leeks in a broiler-safe dish, broil for 1 minute or until the breadcrumbs are toasted (don't let it burn!).

Notes

  • If doubling the recipe, use 2 large skillets so the mushrooms get a chance to brown instead of stewing.
  • If you have time, let the mushrooms sit out uncovered for 30-60 minutes to dry after washing.
  • Leftover mushroom and leeks can be added to an egg mixture to make a mushroom quiche or this mushroom leek soup. If you're planning on making soup or quiche, I recommend doubling the recipe so you have more mushroom mixture to work with.
  • The nutrition facts are estimated assuming 4 small equal portions without added broiled toppings, though we can easily eat this in 2 servings.
